issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address calls verify_signature but never asserts the result
issues.detail: In chia/_tests/wallet/rpc/test_wallet_rpc.py the new test signs a message by address, then calls client.verify_signature(...) and discards the return value. There is no assert res.isValid (or equivalent). The test would pass even if the RPC returned isValid=False with an error message, which defeats the purpose of adding the test. Add `res = await ...verify_signature(...)` and assert `res.isValid is True` (and ideally `res.error is None`).

issues.description: Name collision and split meaning of `signing_mode_enum` in wallet_request_types.py
issues.detail: The module defines a free function `signing_mode_enum(request)` AND a property `signing_mode_enum` on SignMessageByAddress, SignMessageByID, and VerifySignature. The VerifySignature property does something fundamentally different (parses an optional string field, raises on bad values) from the others (computes from is_hex/safe_mode booleans). Sharing the identifier across three classes with two different semantics makes the code harder to read and grep. Consider renaming the VerifySignature variant (e.g. `parsed_signing_mode`) or making the helper function private (`_signing_mode_from_flags`).

issues.description: `Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic` is an instance method that ignores `self`
issues.detail: The new helper in chia/wallet/wallet.py takes no instance state — it just calls `calculate_synthetic_secret_key(secret_key, DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH)`. Anchoring it on the `Wallet` class and then calling it via `main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...)` in the RPC adds an indirection that obscures the call site (RPC code reads as if it depends on the main wallet, when it doesn't). Make it a `@staticmethod`, or better, a free function in chia/wallet/util/signing.py next to `sign_message`.

issues.description: Stale docstring in verify_signature after refactor
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py:23-27 documents `:param request:` but the function signature was refactored to take individual keyword arguments (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address). The docstring is a copy-paste from the old RPC handler. Update it to document the actual parameters.

issues.description: Address-mismatch error in verify_signature masks signature-invalid error
issues.detail: In chia/wallet/util/signing.py, when `address is not None` and the puzzle hash does not match expected, the function returns `error="Public key doesn't match the address"` regardless of whether the signature itself is valid. If the caller passed both a bad signature and a wrong address, only the address mismatch is reported. This matches the prior behavior, so it is not a regression — but the refactor was a good moment to consider whether returning both pieces of information (or short-circuiting before AugSchemeMPL.verify) would be cleaner. Flagging as preserved smell.

issues.description: Mode dispatch logic is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature
issues.detail: Both `sign_message` and `verify_signature` in chia/wallet/util/signing.py contain near-identical if/elif chains over SigningMode that build the bytes to sign/verify. The dispatches differ subtly: sign treats `CHIP_0002_HEX_INPUT` as a distinct tree-hashed path while verify lumps `CHIP_0002` and `CHIP_0002_P2_DELEGATED_CONDITIONS` together. Factoring out a single `message_bytes_for_mode(mode, message, *, hex_input)` helper would make the asymmetry explicit and prevent future drift. (Preserves existing behavior — not a correctness issue today.)

issues.description: `request.signing_mode_enum` is recomputed multiple times per RPC call
issues.detail: In chia/wallet/wallet_rpc_api.py sign_message_by_address and sign_message_by_id, the `signing_mode_enum` property is accessed twice (and three times in the DID/NFT branches: once when passing `mode=...` and once for the response `signing_mode=request.signing_mode_enum.value`). It is pure and cheap, but readers may not realize it's a property, and binding it to a local once is idiomatic.

issues.description: Inconsistent keyword-only vs positional argument style in signing.py
issues.detail: `verify_signature` uses `*` to force keyword-only arguments; `sign_message` uses positional. Both are public helpers in the same module. Picking one convention (probably keyword-only for both, given the number of args and the type-confusable str/bytes/G1Element/G2Element mix) would improve consistency.

issues.description: signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types, coupling a util to a request-types module
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports `VerifySignatureResponse` from chia/wallet/wallet_request_types.py. This makes the util depend on the request/response surface, which is the opposite of the usual layering (request types depend on utils, not vice versa). Today there is no cycle, but if anything in wallet_request_types ever needs to call into signing, it will break. Consider defining a small VerifyResult dataclass in signing.py and converting at the RPC boundary, mirroring SignMessageResponse.

issues.description: Two extra awaits per call in sign_message_by_id
issues.detail: The old DIDWallet.sign_message resolved the p2 puzzle hash and signed in a single coroutine. The new code awaits `did_wallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash()`, then awaits `wallet_state_manager.get_private_key(...)`, then awaits `did_wallet.get_coin()`, then calls sign_message. Functionally equivalent but slightly more chatty. Not a problem in practice.

positions.position: Move it to chia/wallet/util/signing.py as a free function — it has no instance state and the new util module is the natural home; calling it via `main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...)` in the RPC is misleading.
Leave it on Wallet for now — it's an internal helper, callers already have a wallet handy, and moving it could ripple into more sites. Cleanup is a P2 follow-up, not a blocker.

dissents.topic: Address-mismatch vs signature-invalid error precedence in verify_signature

positions.position: The function reports only one of two possible errors when both are present. Either short-circuit the address check before AugSchemeMPL.verify (cheaper, clearer), or aggregate both errors into the response.

This is a behavior-preserving refactor PR; changing the error precedence — even toward something cleaner — could break clients that pattern-match on `error == "Public key doesn't match the address"`. Leave it.

Rename to clarify intent: the VerifySignature property parses a stringly-typed enum (`parsed_signing_mode`), while SignMessageBy{Address,ID} compute from booleans (`signing_mode_from_flags`). Same name for two semantics is a code smell.

Three call sites all use `request.signing_mode_enum` — having one shared property name across request types makes the RPC handler symmetrical and easier to template. The naming is fine if the property docstring explains it.

review.summary: This PR is a behavior-preserving refactor that extracts message signing/verification from the wallet RPC into chia/wallet/util/signing.py and adds tests for sign_message_by_id (NFT path) and sign_message_by_address. The logic was moved faithfully — I found no P0 issues. The main concrete defect is P1: `test_sign_message_by_address` calls `verify_signature` but does not assert the response, so it would pass even if verification failed. Remaining findings are P2: a confusing `signing_mode_enum` name overloaded across three classes (with two different semantics on VerifySignature vs SignMessageBy*), `Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic` being an instance method that ignores self (better as a free function in signing.py), a stale `:param request:` docstring on verify_signature, duplicated mode-dispatch logic between sign_message and verify_signature, and an upward import of VerifySignatureResponse into the util layer. None of these block merge once the missing assertion is added.
